npcs.name: Arjun Menon
npcs.bio: 21, guitarist, terrible at eating before gigs. Earnest, funny, wants to teach music someday.

npcs.name: Nila Varghese
npcs.bio: 21, design student, photographs hands instead of faces. Dry wit, fierce about her work.

locations.name: The Copper Mug
locations.description: Live music, overpriced drinks, decent mocktails. 21+.

actions.label: Drinks with friends
actions.description: A couple of beers and loud conversation.

actions.label: Mocktails & karaoke
actions.description: All of the fun, none of the hangover.

actions.label: Smoke break
actions.description: Five minutes of relief. A lifetime of interest.

interviewModifiers.reason: Background check: a police case on record

achievements.title: Designated Friend
achievements.description: Stayed sober to look after everyone.

achievements.title: Friends Don't Let Friends
achievements.description: Took the keys from a drunk friend.

epilogueLines.text: There's a police case on your record now. It follows you into every background check — but records are not the whole of a person, and you know it.
The leaked paper cost you more than ₹2,000. Trust, it turns out, is slow to re-earn and quick to spend.
You quit smoking before it quit you. Your lungs — and Amma — are grateful.
You still smoke. It's ₹1,500 a month and a little breath at a time. Quitting is always an option.
Drinking takes more of your weekends — and your money — than you admit. The people who love you have noticed.
Arjun plays you a new song every time you visit. Most are about you. Some are about food.
Nila's first exhibition has one portrait with a face in it. It's yours.
You and your ex still send each other birthday wishes. Some endings are done well.
You never get on a bike with someone who's been drinking again. Not once.

events.title: Culture Fest
events.summary: The college culture fest — music, photographs and new people.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The culture fest takes over campus: a band soundchecking on the main stage, a photo-walk sign-up desk, food stalls selling everything fried. Two people keep crossing your path tonight.

choices.label: Stick with your own friends all night.

arjun.speaker: arjun
arjun.text: Arjun Menon, 21, plays guitar for the closing act and is too nervous to eat. You talk him through it; he plays well and finds you afterwards to say thanks. 'Same time next fest?'

nila.speaker: nila
nila.text: Nila Varghese, 21, runs the photography club and photographs strangers' hands, never faces. She shows you her favourite shot of the night. It's your hands, holding a paper cup of chai.

friends.speaker: narrator
friends.text: You dance badly with your friends until the generator gives up. Some nights don't need to be anything more.

events.title: Something More?
events.summary: Do you want to ask someone out? (Completely optional.)

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: You've been thinking about someone more than usual. Romance is entirely optional — some people want a partner at twenty, some don't, both are fine.

choices.label: Ask Arjun out for coffee.
choices.hint: Only works if the feeling is mutual.

choices.label: Ask Nila out for coffee.
choices.hint: Only works if the feeling is mutual.

choices.label: Not looking for romance right now.

yes_arjun.speaker: arjun
yes_arjun.text: Arjun says yes before you've finished the question, then blushes about it. Coffee turns into a long walk. You're dating now — carefully, happily, at your own pace.

onEnter.text: Your first date: coffee that became a three-hour walk.

yes_nila.speaker: nila
yes_nila.text: Nila smiles slowly. 'I was going to ask you next week. You beat me.' You're dating now — no rush, no labels you don't both want.

onEnter.text: Your first date: she photographed the rain instead of you, then you.

no.speaker: narrator
no.text: They say no — kindly, clearly. 'I like you a lot. Just not like that.' It stings. It's also theirs to decide, and you thank them for being honest. The friendship survives, maybe even stronger.

none.speaker: narrator
none.text: You let the thought go. Your life is already full, and that's a choice too.

events.title: Two Places at Once
events.summary: Your partner's birthday lands on a hard day.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Your partner's birthday is on Friday. So is a deadline you've been dreading — and, if you have one, a café shift you promised to cover.

choices.label: Explain honestly and plan a proper celebration for Sunday.

celebrate.speaker: narrator
celebrate.text: Candles, cheap cake, very good company. Your deadline suffers a little. You'd do it again.

honest.speaker: narrator
honest.text: 'Sunday it is,' they say, and mean it. Sunday turns out to be the best day of the month.

forgot.speaker: narrator
forgot.text: A quiet message on Saturday: 'it's fine.' It isn't, quite. Some things you have to rebuild.

events.title: What Are We?
events.summary: Distance, futures and a real conversation.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Final term changes every conversation. Jobs in different cities, families asking questions, a future that won't stay vague. Your partner asks what you want.

choices.label: Commit — distance or not, you want this.

then.text: You chose each other, on purpose.

else.text: You chose each other, on purpose.

choices.label: Keep it going, but no big promises yet.
End it kindly — your lives are pulling in different directions.

commit.speaker: narrator
commit.text: You say it out loud, which is the hard part. The rest — train tickets, video calls, two families' opinions — you'll solve together.

slow.speaker: narrator
slow.text: 'Okay,' they say. 'One semester at a time.' It's honest. It's enough for now.

end.speaker: narrator
end.text: It's the kindest hard conversation you've ever had. You both cry a bit, then share the last samosa. Some endings are done well.

events.title: Tea Stall Break
events.summary: Friends pass around cigarettes at the tea stall.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Between classes, the gang gathers at the tea stall behind the bus stop. Someone holds out a packet. 'Just one, machan. Relax.'

choices.label: Decline and change the subject with a terrible joke.

hooked.speaker: narrator
hooked.text: It tastes awful. The next one tastes less awful. Within a month you're buying your own packets, and the tea stall uncle knows your brand.

once.speaker: narrator
once.text: You cough, everyone laughs, and you decide once was enough. Mostly.

no.speaker: narrator
no.text: Nobody really cares. Peer pressure is louder in your head than in real life.

events.title: The Cough
events.summary: Your smoking is catching up with you.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: You get breathless climbing the stairs to the bus stand. That evening Amma finds a packet in your bag and puts it on the table without a word. That's worse than shouting.

choices.label: Buy nicotine patches and quit properly (₹2,000).

quit.speaker: narrator
quit.text: The first week is irritable, the second is boring, the third is quietly triumphant. You've quit. Amma buys you a box of sweets and says nothing about it, which says everything.

relapse.speaker: narrator
relapse.text: You last nine days. Then a bad afternoon, a borrowed cigarette, and you're back. Quitting often takes more than one try — you can try again.

later.speaker: amma
later.text: 'Soon,' Amma repeats, in the voice she uses for 'never'.

events.title: The Seniors' Party
events.summary: A party with plenty of alcohol and plenty of pressure.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A senior's flat, loud music, a kitchen counter full of bottles. Someone presses a glass into your hand.

choices.label: Have one drink and pace yourself.
Stay sober and look after your friends.

variants.text: You're under 21 — the legal drinking age here. Wardens and parents have long memories.

one.speaker: narrator
one.text: One drink, lots of water, good conversations on the balcony. You get home at a sensible hour feeling like an adult.

hangover.speaker: narrator
hangover.text: The next morning feels like a construction site inside your skull. You miss your first class and most of your dignity.

trouble.speaker: narrator
trouble.text: Somewhere between the third and fifth drink, your phone disappears. Replacing it costs ₹6,000 you'd planned for other things.

warden.speaker: narrator
warden.text: The hostel warden is waiting at the gate with a register. Your name goes in it, and a letter goes home. Amma calls. It is a long call.

sober.speaker: narrator
sober.text: You spend the night refilling water glasses, finding lost shoes and booking autos. Three people text you thanks the next day.

leave.speaker: narrator
leave.text: You're in bed by eleven. Some of the stories you missed sound fun; most sound like you made the right call.

events.title: Too Many Nights
events.summary: Your drinking has become a pattern.

start.speaker: kavya
start.text: Kavya says it first, carefully: 'You've been drunk four weekends out of five. I'm not judging. I'm worried.' Your bank statement says something similar, less carefully.

choices.label: Cut down: weekends only, two-drink limit.

cut.speaker: narrator
cut.text: It's easier than you feared and harder than you hoped. Your mornings come back first.

help.speaker: narrator
help.text: The counsellor is unshockable and kind. You leave with a plan, a phone number, and less shame than you walked in with.

deny.speaker: narrator
deny.text: Kavya drops it. The drinks don't. The cost shows up every month — in money, in mornings, in how people look at you.

events.title: A Ride Home
events.summary: A friend who's been drinking offers to drive you home.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Midnight. Your friend jingles his bike keys. He's had four drinks and insists he's 'totally fine'.

choices.label: Refuse, and take an auto home.
Take his keys and put you both in an auto.

safe.speaker: narrator
safe.text: The auto driver plays old Ilaiyaraaja songs all the way home. Best ₹350 you ever spent.

keys.speaker: narrator
keys.text: He's furious for ten minutes and grateful for ten years.

lucky.speaker: narrator
lucky.text: You get home. Nothing happened. You lie awake anyway, thinking about how easily something could have.

crash.speaker: narrator
crash.text: A pothole, a skid, and the road arrives very fast. Two weeks in a cast and a hospital bill. It could have been far worse; you know that every time you see a bike.

events.title: The Leaked Paper
events.summary: Someone is selling the semester question paper.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A WhatsApp message from an unknown number: 'Sem paper. 100% genuine. ₹2,000. Limited.' Half your class seems to have received it.

choices.label: Report it to the exam cell anonymously.

got_away.speaker: narrator
got_away.text: The paper is genuine. You do well. You also find you can't quite enjoy the grade, and you notice how many classmates now trust you less than they did.

caught.speaker: narrator
caught.text: The exam cell traces the payments. Malpractice: your paper is cancelled, you'll repeat it as a backlog, and the incident goes on your file. Mr. Fernandes hears about it. He doesn't say anything. He doesn't have to.

onEnter.text: You were caught buying a leaked paper.

ignore.speaker: narrator
ignore.text: You study the old way. The rumour later turns out to be half true, half scam. You're glad you never found out which half you'd have bought.

report.speaker: narrator
report.text: Two days later the exam is rescheduled with a new paper. Nobody knows who reported it. Mr. Fernandes, somehow, gives you a very slight nod.

events.title: No Bills, No Questions
events.summary: An easy-money offer that's too easy.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Shiva, a friend of a friend, has a bag of brand-new phones with no boxes and no bills. 'You sell them to your college crowd, we split fifty-fifty. Twelve thousand for you, easy.' Nobody asks where they came from. That's the point.

choices.label: Do it — you need the money.
Walk away, and warn Kavya not to buy anything from him.

effects.text: You warned her about stolen phones.

clean.speaker: narrator
clean.text: Every phone sells in a week. The money's real. So is the knot in your stomach whenever a police jeep passes.

raid.speaker: narrator
raid.text: Three weeks later the police raid Shiva's room and find your number everywhere. Receiving and selling stolen property: a case is filed. A lawyer, a fine and months of court dates follow, and your family finds out the worst way.

onEnter.text: You got involved in a police case.

no.speaker: narrator
no.text: Shiva shrugs and finds someone else. A month later you hear he's been arrested.

warn.speaker: narrator
warn.text: Kavya had already been offered a 'cheap' phone. She sends you a single word: 'thanks'. A month later Shiva is arrested.

events.title: Stopped at the Signal
events.summary: No licence, no helmet, one traffic constable.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: You're riding a friend's scooter — no helmet, licence at home. A constable waves you over.

choices.label: Accept the official fine and get a receipt (₹1,000).
Argue that you were 'only going nearby'.

fine.speaker: narrator
fine.text: The receipt is printed on paper thinner than a samosa wrapper. You buy a helmet the same evening.

bribe.speaker: narrator
bribe.text: He pockets it without looking at you. It worked. It also cost something that isn't on any receipt.

caught.speaker: narrator
caught.text: An inspector was watching. Offering a bribe turns a ₹1,000 fine into a case. You spend a terrible afternoon at the station before a stern warning and a much bigger fine.

argue.speaker: narrator
argue.text: He listens, nods, and writes the fine anyway. Arguing is free; it's just not useful.

events.title: Fantasy Cricket Riches
events.summary: A betting app promises easy money.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A friend shows you his screen: ₹40,000 won on an online betting app 'in one night'. He doesn't show you the screens from the other nights.

win.speaker: narrator
win.text: You win ₹6,000. Your heart races for an hour. The app immediately suggests a bigger bet. That's how it works.

lose.speaker: narrator
lose.text: The team collapses in the final over and so does your ₹3,000. The app sends you a 'better luck next time' bonus to try again. That's how it works.

skip.speaker: narrator
skip.text: The match is just as exciting without money on it. More, even — you can enjoy both teams' good shots.

events.title: Closing Time
events.summary: Someone won't take no for an answer.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: At The Copper Mug, a drunk man keeps bothering Kavya after she's told him twice to leave her alone. He grabs her wrist.

choices.label: Step between them and wave over the bouncer.

effects.text: You stood up for her — and kept your head.

choices.label: Pull Kavya away and leave together.

bouncer.speaker: kavya
bouncer.text: The bouncer removes him in under a minute. Kavya is shaken but fine. 'Thank you for not making it worse,' she says, which is a strange and accurate compliment.

leave.speaker: narrator
leave.text: You walk her home. Neither of you goes back to that bar.

bruised.speaker: narrator
bruised.text: It's over in seconds. You have a split lip and a sprained hand; he has a bloody nose. The manager throws you both out.

police.speaker: narrator
police.text: Someone calls the police. Both of you spend the night at the station, and a case is registered for the fight. Kavya waits outside until morning.
